keyVerseText: In his days did Hiel the Bethelite build Jericho: he laid the foundation thereof in Abiram his firstborn, and set up the gates thereof in his youngest son Segub, according to the word of the LORD, which he spake by Joshua the son of Nun.
rootMeaning: The Hebrew noun שְׂגוּב (Sᵉgûwb) derives from the root שָׂגַב (sâgab), which carries the sense of being lofty, exalted, or set on high. This root conveys ideas of strength, protection, and inaccessibility, both literally and figuratively. Thus, the name שְׂגוּב not only identifies a person but also embodies the concept of exaltation and being elevated above, emphasizing a position of honor or security beyond mere earthly status.
usageInScripture: The word שְׂגוּב appears three times in Scripture, exclusively as a proper name referring to two Israelites: the youngest son of Hiel the Bethelite who rebuilt Jericho, and a Judaite descendant of Hezron. Its translations consistently reflect its function as a personal name, such as "son Segub" or "him Segub," highlighting that its primary biblical use is nominative rather than descriptive. This consistency underscores the significance of names in Hebrew Scripture as carriers of meaning related to identity and divine purpose.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding שְׂגוּב in its original sense of exaltation enriches our appreciation for biblical names as more than labels; they often signify God's providential plan and character traits to be emulated. The exalted nature implied by שְׂגוּב points to the believer’s calling to be set apart and elevated in Christ, reflecting spiritual security and strength rooted in God. This aligns with the biblical theme that God lifts up the humble and establishes His people on high, reminding Christians of their identity in Christ as exalted and protected by divine power.
keyVerseReflection: 1 Kings 16:34 records that Hiel the Bethelite rebuilt Jericho, laying its foundation and setting up its gates "in his youngest son Segub," fulfilling the word of the LORD spoken through Joshua. The use of the name שְׂגוּב here is poignant, as it connects the act of rebuilding and restoration with the notion of exaltation and strength embedded in the name. This highlights how God's sovereign word works through human history, raising up individuals and acts to accomplish His divine purposes, even amid challenging circumstances.
